question: Who is the author of the book 'From Plassey to Partition and After: A History of Modern India'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sekhar Bandyopadhyay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Sekhar Bandyopadhyay** is a prominent historian and academician known for his extensive work on modern Indian history.

• He is a Professor of Asian History at **Victoria University of Wellington** in New Zealand.

• The book **'From Plassey to Partition and After: A History of Modern India'** offers a comprehensive analysis of the history of modern India, starting from the Battle of Plassey in 1757 to the post-Independence era.

• This book is widely used in academic circles and is considered an essential resource for understanding the complexities of Indian history during the colonial and post-colonial periods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Romila Thapar**

• Romila Thapar is a renowned Indian historian whose principal area of study is ancient India.

• She is an Emerita Professor of History at the Jawaharlal Nehru University in New Delhi.

• Her notable works include "A History of India," "Early India: From the Origins to AD 1300," and "The Past Before Us."

• **David Hardiman**

• David Hardiman is a British historian and a founding member of the Subaltern Studies group.

• His works focus on the history of Indian nationalism and the role of the peasantry in the Indian independence movement.

• Some of his significant works include "Peasant Resistance in India 1858-1914" and "Gandhi in His Time and Ours."

• **Sumit Sarkar**

• Sumit Sarkar is an Indian historian who has contributed extensively to the field of modern Indian history.

• He is known for his work on the Swadeshi movement and the history of the Indian left.

• His notable books include "Modern India: 1885-1947" and "Writing Social History."
